claims.statement: OpenWiki's per-user state directory root is resolved once at startup to ~/.openwiki by default, but the OPENWIKI_CONFIG_DIR environment variable overrides it, with a leading ~ expanded to the home directory.

ensureOpenWikiHome creates the home directory and its managed subdirectories (connectors, conversation_history, wiki, skills) with mode 0o700, re-chmods the home directory to 0o700, and applies restrictDirToCurrentUser so the state directory is owner-only across platforms; it only ever mkdirs (recursive, so a pre-existing directory is a no-op) and chmods, never moving, renaming, or deleting an existing ~/.openwiki, so operator files survive setup and a re-run never destroys a configured home.

ensureConnectorHome validates a connector id against ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$ and creates the connector's directory plus raw/ and logs/ subdirectories at mode 0o700, and resolveConnectorRawPath rejects relative paths that would escape the connector's raw directory.
Provider credentials and model configuration are persisted to ~/.openwiki/.env, where the env directory is the OpenWiki home directory itself.

saveOpenWikiEnv serializes writes through an internal queue that is reset after a failed save, writes the credential file to a same-directory temp file at 0o600 and atomically renames it into place to avoid truncation, and drops empty values rather than persisting KEY="".
saveOpenWikiEnv does not overwrite a key present in the launch shell environment within process.env, treating the saved value only as a fallback for when the shell variable is unset.

buildCredentialEnvUpdates is a pure function that computes the ~/.openwiki/.env update map from wizard-collected values (provider, primary credential, base URL, secret key, region, GCP project/location, model id, reasoning effort, LangSmith key) and performs no IO, leaving persistence to saveOpenWikiEnv.
buildCredentialEnvUpdates writes the provider key only when it differs from the current environment, so re-running setup with the same provider does not churn the .env file.

A non-empty LangSmith key also sets LANGCHAIN_PROJECT=openwiki and LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2=true, while a blank LangSmith input sets LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2=false to explicitly disable tracing rather than leaving an earlier true value in place.

orderedSetupSteps returns the wizard's steps in walk order for a given provider and run mode: an optional run-mode chooser, the provider, its primary credential step, provider-specific steps (secret key, GCP project/location, base URL, region), the model step, the LangSmith step, and a code-repo-confirm step only in code mode.

credentialStep selects a provider's primary credential step by auth style: oauth-login for OAuth providers, no step for AWS-SDK providers, external-cli-auth for external-CLI providers, api-key for API-key providers, and gcp-project for keyless providers that require a GCP project.

getInitialStep is a skip-based waterfall that lands on the first unsatisfied setup step, but when walkAll (explicit --init) is set it starts at the top and walks every applicable step even ones already configured.

needsCredentialSetup returns true when the provider is invalid or any required credential/model/LangSmith input is missing, and otherwise returns whether onboarding is incomplete for the mode (repository code onboarding for code mode, personal onboarding otherwise).

Onboarding state is persisted as version-1 JSON at ~/.openwiki/onboarding.json recording completedAt, run mode, source instances, ingestion schedule, power management, and template metadata, and saveOpenWikiOnboardingConfig writes it at mode 0o600 and re-chmods it to 0o600.

normalizeOnboardingConfig repairs partial or legacy onboarding shapes: it accepts legacy templateId/templateName as fallbacks for modeId/modeName, drops unknown connector ids, migrates the legacy sources map into sourceInstances, lifts a per-source schedule to the top-level ingestionSchedule, and re-derives the legacy sources map from the normalized instances.

The wiki brief (wikiGoal) is stored outside onboarding.json: saveOpenWikiOnboardingConfig strips wikiGoal from the JSON and writes it to a separate INSTRUCTIONS.md file at 0o600, and readOpenWikiOnboardingConfig re-attaches it by reading that file back.
isOnboardingComplete requires a completedAt timestamp, a non-empty wikiGoal, and either a code-mode config or a present ingestion schedule.

The synchronous completion checks read the wiki brief from different locations by mode: isOpenWikiOnboardingCompleteSync reads ~/.openwiki/INSTRUCTIONS.md, while isRepositoryCodeOnboardingCompleteSync requires a code-mode config and reads the brief from the target repository.

In code mode the wiki brief is written to <repo>/openwiki/INSTRUCTIONS.md at mode 0o644 via saveRepositoryWikiInstructions, and the setup controller saves onboarding.json with wikiGoal cleared so the brief lives with the repository rather than in the home directory.

The default code-mode target repository is the nearest ancestor of the working directory containing a .git directory (findNearestGitRepoRoot), falling back to the current directory when none is found.

ensureCodeModeRepoSetup bootstraps a code-mode repository by refreshing the managed AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md snippets and, only when createWorkflow is set, creating the scheduled-update workflow; it is invoked before both CLI print/interactive runs and durable repository runs.

writeCodeModeAgentSnippets creates AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md when missing and otherwise replaces only the content between the <!-- OPENWIKI:START --> and <!-- OPENWIKI:END --> markers, preparing and validating both files before writing either and aborting with the file unchanged when markers are malformed or duplicated. A CLAUDE.md whose trimmed content is exactly @AGENTS.md (CLAUDE_AGENTS_IMPORT) is left unchanged (nextContent undefined). When CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md resolve to the same file on disk (e.g. CLAUDE.md is a symlink to AGENTS.md, detected by resolvesToSameFile via matching inode and device), the CLAUDE.md snippet carries the full instructions inline (the same snippet as AGENTS.md) instead of the @AGENTS.md pointer, because the import would point the file at itself; otherwise the CLAUDE.md snippet is the minimal @AGENTS.md pointer. A CLAUDE.md with marker regions or other content is refreshed in place.

The scheduled-update workflow is created only under the init command and only when .github/workflows/openwiki-update.yml does not already exist, so --update and chat runs, and re-runs over an existing file, never overwrite operator customizations.

createCodeModeWorkflow emits a workflow_dispatch-plus-scheduled GitHub Actions job running openwiki code --update --print on a default cron of 0 8 * * *, with contents/pull-requests write permissions; it pins actions to commit SHAs (actions/checkout v4 with fetch-depth 0, actions/setup-node v4 on Node 22, peter-evans/create-pull-request v7), installs openwiki plus optional mermaid/jsdom, runs with continue-on-error so a page failure does not abort, deletes openwiki/.run.json, opens a PR scoped to openwiki/AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/the workflow file even on failure, and a final step exits 1 when steps.openwiki.outcome == 'failure' to propagate the failure.

createWorkflowProviderEnv derives the workflow provider env block from the operator's configured provider, wiring secrets through secrets., non-sensitive settings (base URL, project, region) through vars., quoting the model id (some IDs like Cloudflare Workers AI's leading @ are not plain YAML scalars), and emitting a comment for OAuth providers instead of pinning a short-lived rotated token; an opted-in OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_STREAMING override is also propagated.

The .openwikiignore file governs which repository paths the doc agent may read/edit; rules are applied in file order with last-match-wins semantics so a later negated (!) rule can re-include an excluded path, and matching is case-insensitive to prevent alternate-cased bypasses on case-insensitive filesystems.

For non-interactive runs (--print or no TTY) resolveStartupCommand fails fast with an actionable error when the configured provider is missing a required credential, and requires a TTY for interactive chat, but allows a clean update --print no-op to proceed without credentials.

The setup wizard offers two run modes, Personal (a local personal brain wiki built in ~/.openwiki/wiki) and Code (repository documentation in ./openwiki), with code mode's default source being a local Git repository plus LangSmith.

beginRepositoryRun validates the requested --language value before touching the repository, rejecting an unrecognized BCP-47 tag (via resolveLanguage) rather than silently defaulting to English, because a wrong language would be persisted in durable run state and a later resume refuses to change a started run's language.

The LangSmith code-mode connector separates committed shared config from the secret key: saveLangSmithSetup writes openwiki/.langsmith.json whose workspaces name apiKeyEnv (the env var name), projects (trimmed/deduped, order preserved), and an optional apiBaseUrl for non-US regions; the API key itself is never committed, only the env var name that points at it. During setup a freshly-entered workspace key is written to ~/.openwiki/.env under that workspace's apiKeyEnv, and at pull time the connector reads process.env[apiKeyEnv].

A LangSmith key is workspace- and region-bound, so each workspace gets its own key env var: OPENWIKI_LANGSMITH_API_KEY for the first, then OPENWIKI_LANGSMITH_API_KEY_2, _3, ... assigned by nextLangSmithApiKeyEnv. Region is chosen in-wizard (US/EU/APAC via LANGSMITH_REGION_OPTIONS) and maps to an allowlisted official host written into apiBaseUrl (US is the connector default, so it is omitted from the file).

Two hard guardrails keep a committed .langsmith.json from exfiltrating secrets or escaping the LangSmith surface: sanitizeLangSmithApiKeyEnv accepts an apiKeyEnv only when it matches ^OPENWIKI_LANGSMITH_API_KEY(_[A-Z0-9]+)?$ (so a malicious PR cannot name an unrelated secret), and sanitizeLangSmithApiBaseUrl accepts a base URL only when it is https, carries no embedded credentials, and targets one of the three official LangSmith hosts (otherwise dropped to prevent SSRF/key exfiltration). A workspace failing either allowlist or any shape check is dropped, not fatal, so one bad entry does not invalidate the whole config.

The committed LangSmith config is WYSIWYG and touch-gated: saveLangSmithSetup is called at the final step only when langsmithSourcesTouched is true (the LangSmith sub-menu was opened this run), so an untouched setup never rewrites openwiki/.langsmith.json; a workspace with no projects is dropped (which also removes it), and switching a workspace back to US drops its apiBaseUrl.

openwiki --init (code) and openwiki personal --init always open the full setup walk even when already configured, gated by initWizardConsumed so the walk opens once and does not re-open on a later return to idle; needsCredentialSetup independently opens the wizard for any run (including chat) when the provider is invalid or a required credential/model/LangSmith input is missing.

At the final step the setup controller persists in order: buildCredentialEnvUpdates computes the .env update map (pure) and saveOpenWikiEnv atomically writes it to ~/.openwiki/.env (provider key only when changed, empty values dropped, LangSmith tracing toggled); in code mode, touched LangSmith workspace keys are saved to ~/.openwiki/.env and saveLangSmithSetup writes openwiki/.langsmith.json; saveConfigForCurrentMode writes onboarding.json (completedAt set), and for code mode saveRepositoryWikiInstructions writes the brief to <repo>/openwiki/INSTRUCTIONS.md at 0o644 with wikiGoal cleared from onboarding.json.

When the operator chooses Run ingestion now in code mode, onComplete returns runIngestionNow and the App transitions to init-setup-saved and proceeds into the init run, which calls ensureCodeModeRepoSetup (refreshing AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md and, because the command is init, creating the scheduled-update workflow when absent), pulls code-mode connector evidence (LangSmith traces when configured), and hands the augmented message to the doc agent for the first wiki generation; --init and --update auto-exit on success in an interactive terminal.
